Of 523 names scanned, 185 register STRONG BUY and the concentration is unmistakable: financials and insurance (PNC, USB, BAC, JPM, AIZ, GL, ALL all above 89), aerospace and industrials (HWM, GE, RTX), energy (CVX, LNG, OXY, VLO, PSX, MPC), materials (RS, NUE, ASH) and staples (KO, MDLZ). The companies that BUY compute are making new highs while the companies that make the equipment are being sold: NTAP and SNOW closed at 52-week highs, DELL is up 90% in three months, HPE 77%, ANET scores 90.0, and NVDA still scores 87.9 only 7% off its high with TradingView at BUY. Macro backdrop: Middle East escalation with vessel traffic through Hormuz thinning ahead of Iran-Oman talks, which is a live bid under the energy complex and the reason several refiners and E&Ps score in the 90s. Practical posture: buy the un-extended breakouts in the new leadership, do not chase the RSI-75-plus names into the open, and treat any semiconductor-equipment position as a source of funds rather than a dip to buy. A constructive resolution in the Iran talks would unwind the energy bid quickly — size that group accordingly.
